text: Now, here's the real monster of the deep, and it isn't an animal.
Right now, at the surface, the air is pressing on you with a weight called one atmosphere.
You don't feel it because you were born in it.
But water is much heavier than air.
Every 10 meters you go down, you add one more atmosphere.
At the bottom of the Mariana Trench, that adds up to more than 1,000 atmospheres.
That's like having more than 7 tons pressing on every square inch of your body.
Think of an elephant standing on your thumbnail.
Pressure like that crushes airspaces flat.
A normal military submarine would be crushed long before it got anywhere near the bottom.
So to get a human down there alive, you need a very special machine.
And in 1960, two men climbed into one.
